findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A teammate changes workers from Claude to Codex on the default branch while this checkout is behind. `start` reads the checkout's old `forge.toml` and offers a Claude explorer. A fix is subsequently based on the freshly fetched default branch (`src/forge/task.py:222` and `src/forge/task.py:804`), and the worker uses routed default-branch settings (`src/forge/worker.py:173`), so Codex builds it. Intake needs the same routed settings as the worker. The full Done-when is: An idea is sorted by the family that workers picks, and new and upgraded repos get the new explore defaults, with repos that have their own explore entries keeping them.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - The repository's full pytest command still contains expectations contradicted by this change. `tests/test_codex_reader.py:180` asserts that init writes the old Codex explore model and no Antigravity entry. `tests/test_claude_subagent_defaults.py:75` and `:91` expect missing explore entries to inherit lite, although `src/forge/roles.py:123` now selects the new defaults. The new-client cases in `tests/test_fix_routing.py:203` also expect a native Codex handout while their configured worker is Claude. These tests need to follow the new contract or the suite cannot pass.
findings.title: Gate: Update existing tests for the new explorer behavior

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - When Claude's authentication has expired or its SDK exits on a service error, `_sdk_read` returns a nonzero status and diagnostic stderr (`src/forge/story.py:1023`), but this branch discards the diagnostic, launches it again, and reports that it could not read the explorer's reply. Codex's failed turn status is treated the same way. The user is directed to repeat the same command without being told the actual problem.
Adds work: distinguish provider failures from malformed replies and surface their diagnostics; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Functional: Report provider failures instead of malformed replies

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Scale
Case: normal use - Sorting 100 different ideas in a repository with 200 MiB of eligible files leaves roughly 20 GiB of checkout copies. Each idea gets a distinct hash, and `src/forge/antigravity.py:272` through `:279` copies the checkout into a persistent directory for that target; `copy_for_reading` only removes an earlier copy of the same target. Successful explorations never remove these directories, so disk use grows without bound.
Adds work: clean up the per-idea read copy after the turn; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Scale: Remove Antigravity's per-idea checkout after sorting

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - The named proof writes the same synthetic settings into the checkout and default branch, so it passes despite the current stale-default-branch routing defect. It also never runs init or upgrade and tests a custom entry only for Antigravity; it would pass if init wrote the wrong default or an upgrade discarded an existing Codex entry. The proof list therefore does not establish the full Done-when: An idea is sorted by the family that workers picks, and new and upgraded repos get the new explore defaults, with repos that have their own explore entries keeping them.
findings.title: Test: Prove explorer routing and defaults for new and upgraded repos

why: The explorer does not follow the builder choice: intake.py takes the family from the session, and the explore defaults are gpt-6.2-sol for Codex and none for Antigravity.
